extraction_notes: This is a MetLife 'Benefit Summary' for a group life product (e.g. Supplemental Term Life). Page 1 has a coverage-schedule table with three columns - Employee, Spouse, Child - each showing: Life Coverage Schedule (purchase increment, e.g. 'Increments of $10,000' for Employee, 'Increments of $5,000' for Spouse, or a flat amount like '$10,000' for Child), Non Medical Maximum (guarantee-issue amount), Overall Benefit Maximum (may reference a salary multiple, e.g. 'The lesser of 5 times Your Basic Annual Earnings, or $500,000'), AD&D Coverage (usually 'Yes, same amount as Life coverage' for every class), AD&D Maximum, and Employee Contribution (e.g. '100%'). Page 2 has the actual rate tables: a full age-banded grid for Employee (rows = age bands: Under 30, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70+; columns = coverage amounts, typically $1,000/$10,000/$20,000/$40,000/$50,000/$100,000; cell = monthly premium for that age band at that coverage amount), and a separate, usually IDENTICAL, age-banded grid for Spouse (same age bands and coverage amounts - Spouse premium is based on the EMPLOYEE's age, not the spouse's). Child coverage on page 2 is NOT age-banded - it's a single flat monthly premium for a single flat coverage amount (e.g. '$10,000 -> $2.91/month'), shown in a small separate box next to the Employee table. There are exactly 3 coverage classes total: Employee (age_banded), Spouse (age_banded), Child (flat). Pages 3+ are footnotes, exclusions, portability/conversion terms, and legal disclosures - not needed for extraction. There is typically only ONE product per document (e.g. just 'Supplemental Term Life'), but check for multiple if the group name/plan design section lists more than one.
source: Seeded manually from Bartel Communications Supplemental Term Life benefit summary (MetLife, form L0224038398) processed in chat before the age-banded schema was wired into the app.
